claims.title: Olmec civilisation flourishes
claims.summary: The Olmec arise on the Gulf coast as the first complex society of Mesoamerica, carving colossal stone heads and shaping a cultural template inherited by later peoples.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1200bce-olmec-civilisation-flourishes, claim TL:MEX:event:1200bce:olmec-civilisation-flourishes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Teotihuacan, city of the gods
claims.summary: Teotihuacan grows into a metropolis of monumental pyramids and a planned ceremonial axis, dominating central Mexico before its decline around 550-650 CE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-100-teotihuacan-city-of-the-gods, claim TL:MEX:event:100:teotihuacan-city-of-the-gods, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Classic Maya civilisation
claims.summary: Maya city-states reach their height, producing hieroglyphic writing, advanced calendars, and astronomy, before the southern lowland centres are abandoned by about 900 CE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-250-classic-maya-civilisation, claim TL:MEX:event:250:classic-maya-civilisation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Tenochtitlan
claims.summary: The Mexica establish their capital on an island in Lake Texcoco, the site of present-day Mexico City.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1325-founding-of-tenochtitlan, claim TL:MEX:event:1325:founding-of-tenochtitlan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Triple Alliance
claims.summary: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan ally, inaugurating the tribute empire of the Aztecs across central Mexico.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1428-the-triple-alliance, claim TL:MEX:event:1428:the-triple-alliance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Moctezuma II
claims.summary: Moctezuma II ascends as huey tlatoani, ruling the empire at its territorial peak until the Spanish arrival.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1502-reign-of-moctezuma-ii, claim TL:MEX:event:1502:reign-of-moctezuma-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cortes lands in Mexico
claims.summary: Hernan Cortes arrives on the Gulf coast and marches inland, allying with peoples opposed to Mexica rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1519-cortes-lands-in-mexico, claim TL:MEX:event:1519:cortes-lands-in-mexico, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
claims.summary: After a siege of some three months, the city falls to Cortes and his indigenous allies, ending the Aztec empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1521-fall-of-tenochtitlan, claim TL:MEX:event:1521:fall-of-tenochtitlan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Viceroyalty of New Spain established
claims.summary: Spain formalises colonial government under a viceroy, with Mexico City as the capital of a vast realm.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1535-viceroyalty-of-new-spain-established, claim TL:MEX:event:1535:viceroyalty-of-new-spain-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Grito de Dolores
claims.summary: Miguel Hidalgo calls for rebellion against Spanish rule, beginning the Mexican War of Independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1810-grito-de-dolores, claim TL:MEX:event:1810:grito-de-dolores, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Iturbide sent against Guerrero
claims.summary: Viceroy Juan Ruiz de Apodaca sends the royalist criollo officer Agustin de Iturbide, known for his campaigns against the insurgents of Hidalgo and Morelos, to defeat the rebel forces of Vicente Guerrero in the south.

sources.label: Mexico: A Country Study (Iturbide and the Plan of Iguala; Empire and Early Republic)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1820-iturbide-sent-against-guerrero, claim TL:MEX:event:1820:iturbide-sent-against-guerrero, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Plan of Iguala
claims.summary: At Iguala, Iturbide proclaims three guarantees (independence, the Roman Catholic religion, and equal rights for criollos and peninsulares) and wins the cooperation of the insurgent Vicente Guerrero.

sources.label: Mexico: A Country Study (Iturbide and the Plan of Iguala; Empire and Early Republic)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1821-plan-of-iguala, claim TL:MEX:event:1821:plan-of-iguala, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Cordoba
claims.summary: At the town of Cordoba, Veracruz, Juan O'Donoju, the Spanish political chief of New Spain, and Agustin de Iturbide, commander of the Army of the Three Guarantees, sign treaties that ratify the principles of the Plan of Iguala.

sources.label: Los tratados de Córdoba y la consumación de la independencia
sources.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Gobierno de México

sources.label: Mexico: A Country Study (Iturbide and the Plan of Iguala; Empire and Early Republic)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1821-treaty-of-cordoba, claim TL:MEX:event:1821:treaty-of-cordoba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence consummated
claims.summary: The Army of the Three Guarantees enters Mexico City following the Treaty of Cordoba, ending Spanish rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1821-independence-consummated, claim TL:MEX:event:1821:independence-consummated, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Act of Independence of the Mexican Empire
claims.summary: The day after the Army of the Three Guarantees enters the capital, the Supreme Junta of the Empire declares Mexico a sovereign nation independent of Spain; Agustin de Iturbide's signature heads the act.

sources.label: Acta de Independencia del Imperio Mexicano, 28 de septiembre de 1821 (text)
sources.publisher: Orden Juridico Nacional, Secretaria de Gobernacion (Mexico)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1821-act-of-independence-of-the-mexican-empire, claim TL:MEX:event:1821:act-of-independence-of-the-mexican-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Iturbide made emperor
claims.summary: The day after his troops march through Mexico City in his support, congress names Iturbide constitutional emperor of Mexico, as Agustin I.

sources.label: Mexico: A Country Study (Iturbide and the Plan of Iguala; Empire and Early Republic)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1822-iturbide-made-emperor, claim TL:MEX:event:1822:iturbide-made-emperor, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Iturbide abdicates
claims.summary: Faced with the revolt of Santa Anna and other generals under the Plan of Casa Mata, Iturbide abdicates the throne.

sources.label: Mexico: A Country Study (Iturbide and the Plan of Iguala; Empire and Early Republic)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1823-iturbide-abdicates, claim TL:MEX:event:1823:iturbide-abdicates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First federal republic
claims.summary: The Constitution of 1824 founds the United Mexican States as a federal republic, with Guadalupe Victoria as first president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1824-first-federal-republic, claim TL:MEX:event:1824:first-federal-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mexican-American War
claims.summary: Defeat by the United States costs Mexico roughly half its territory under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1846-mexican-american-war, claim TL:MEX:event:1846:mexican-american-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitution of the Reform
claims.summary: The liberal Constitution of 1857 limits church and army privileges and establishes a bill of rights, deepening conflict between liberals and conservatives.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1857-constitution-of-the-reform, claim TL:MEX:event:1857:constitution-of-the-reform, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the Second Empire
claims.summary: Mexican forces under Juarez defeat the French intervention; Emperor Maximilian is captured and executed, restoring the republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1867-fall-of-the-second-empire, claim TL:MEX:event:1867:fall-of-the-second-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Porfiriato
claims.summary: Porfirio Diaz rules Mexico for over three decades, modernising the economy while entrenching authoritarian government and land inequality.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1876-the-porfiriato, claim TL:MEX:event:1876:the-porfiriato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mexican Revolution
claims.summary: A decade of revolution and civil war overthrows Diaz, costs over a million lives, and produces the Constitution of 1917.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1910-mexican-revolution, claim TL:MEX:event:1910:mexican-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oil nationalisation
claims.summary: President Lazaro Cardenas nationalises the petroleum industry, creating Pemex and asserting economic sovereignty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1938-oil-nationalisation, claim TL:MEX:event:1938:oil-nationalisation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: NAFTA and the Zapatista uprising
claims.summary: The North American Free Trade Agreement takes effect as the Zapatistas rise in Chiapas; a peso crisis follows that December.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-1994-nafta-and-the-zapatista-uprising, claim TL:MEX:event:1994:nafta-and-the-zapatista-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of one-party rule
claims.summary: Vicente Fox's election ends 71 years of uninterrupted PRI government, marking Mexico's democratic alternation of power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mexico: From the Olmec mother-culture and the lake-city of the Mexica to a republic forged in conquest, reform, and revolution.", terralore.co/country/MEX/chronicle#ev-2000-end-of-one-party-rule, claim TL:MEX:event:2000:end-of-one-party-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
